target_customer: Spanish-speaking consumers in Latin America (about 60% Mexico) paying a subscription, plus creators paid by minutes listened
problem: Spanish-language audiobooks and audio content were scarce and poorly monetized for creators; Beek paid creators per minute listened.
business_model: Consumer subscription with creator revenue share per minute listened
product_category: Spanish-language audiobook and audio subscription platform

founders.name: Pamela Valdes
education: University of Texas at Austin, left college (TechCrunch, LSVP)
previous_startups: A previous company sold to Amazon (per YC page; company not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page and LSVP call her a Thiel Fellow (first from Mexico per LSVP, first Latin American per YC) and a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree; TechCrunch says Beek began as a hackathon project in college.

founders.name: Guillermo Sequeira
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2023-02-02) says he joined in 2019 when the company pivoted to audio; LSVP spells the name Sequeria. Not on the YC page.

founders.name: Max Holzheu
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only, with no background.

exit.reason: beek.io is now a farewell page saying over 4 million people listened to nearly 200 million minutes and that Audible acquired a significant part of the Beek Originals catalog; no date or cause stated on the page.

competitors.name: Audible
competitors.what: Amazon's audiobook service, a main channel for Spanish audiobooks in Spain and Latin America

competitors.name: Storytel
competitors.what: Swedish audiobook subscription service expanding to Mexico and Latin America

competitors.name: Scribd
competitors.what: Digital library subscription that launched a Spanish-language service in Mexico with 60,000 plus Spanish titles

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer subscription audio app with a catalog and creator payouts; the hard part was content and growth rather than technology, though it bought AI recommendation company Tamber in 2022.

defensibility.rationale: Exclusive Beek Originals content and creator relationships gave some protection, but Amazon's Audible and Storytel could outspend it, and Audible ultimately took a significant part of the originals catalog.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per beek.io's farewell page, Audible later acquired a significant part of the Beek Originals catalog; the date is not stated.

market_need_then: A 2019 industry report forecast Spanish-language audiobooks surging with subscription platforms as the leading sales model, while Latin America's audiobook market was described as underdeveloped; Beek said its paying subscriber base grew 18x in the two years before its Series A.

branding.domain_note: beek.io is the product and farewell domain; no purchase history found. BEEK is a registered US trademark of Beek Technologies, Inc. (filed March 2021, registered April 2025).

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission framed as financially viable storytelling for creators and the Latin American Dream

branding.brand_signature: Beek Originals, an exclusive catalog of audio series by independent creators
branding.community_and_virality: Creator-led content with named celebrity creators (for example Lorena Ochoa and Oso Trava invested); a Contxto piece and TechCrunch coverage but no fan or merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press, a farewell page citing 4 million listeners, celebrity creators and high-profile angels suggest solid regional awareness, but no evidence of wider community or merch.

pivots.from: Earlier product at the YC Winter 2017 batch (not described in the sources found)
pivots.why: TechCrunch says Guillermo Sequeira joined in 2019 when the company pivoted to audio

outcome_analysis: Beek raised about $20 million by TechCrunch's figures, grew to over 4 million listeners and nearly 200 million minutes, then closed as a standalone service, with Audible acquiring a significant part of the originals catalog according to the company's farewell page. The reason and date of the shutdown are not public, so no failure factor is assigned. The company competed against Audible and Storytel in a market with limited audiobook spending.
notes: Pre-seed and seed amounts come from one TechCrunch article that gives no seed investors or pre-seed date; the pre-seed amount of $2 million and the seed of about $5 million sum with the Series A to about $20 million, whereas CB Insights lists a total of $13.22M. LSVP says Lightspeed first invested in 2022 while TechCrunch dates the Series A to February 2023. The YC page says founded 2019 but other sources say 2014 or 2015; the batch is Winter 2017, so the original company predates the audio pivot. The farewell page on beek.io is undated, and a search for shutdown coverage found nothing, so the exit date is unknown. Competitor dates are from a March 2019 Publishing Perspectives report URL and an undated Publishers Weekly article, chosen because the audio product started in 2019. Search results on layoffs returned unrelated Audible and Wondery news.
